questions.stem: Which blood vessel carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart?
questions.explanation: The pulmonary vein is one of the two exceptions to the usual pattern: it is a vein, so it carries blood towards the heart, but the blood is oxygenated because it has just come from the lungs. It empties into the left atrium.

distractorRationale.a: The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood away from the heart to the lungs
distractorRationale.c: The aorta carries oxygenated blood away from the heart to the body
distractorRationale.d: The vena cava brings deoxygenated blood from the body to the right atrium

questions.stem: The wall of the left ventricle is thicker than that of the right ventricle because the left ventricle

options.text: holds more blood than the right ventricle
must generate enough pressure to pump blood around the whole body
receives blood at a higher pressure from the left atrium
contains valves that the right ventricle lacks

questions.explanation: The right ventricle only has to push blood a short distance to the nearby lungs, where delicate capillaries would be damaged by high pressure. The left ventricle must drive blood to the brain, limbs and every organ, so it needs far more muscle to develop the necessary pressure.

distractorRationale.a: Both ventricles hold approximately the same volume of blood
distractorRationale.c: Both atria deliver blood at similarly low pressure
distractorRationale.d: Both ventricles have an inlet valve and an outlet semilunar valve

questions.stem: Blood flows from the right atrium into the right ventricle through the
questions.explanation: The tricuspid valve, named for its three flaps, guards the opening between the right atrium and the right ventricle and prevents blood being forced back into the atrium when the ventricle contracts. The corresponding valve on the left side has two flaps and is the bicuspid valve.

distractorRationale.a: The bicuspid valve lies between the left atrium and the left ventricle
distractorRationale.c: Semilunar valves guard the exits into the aorta and pulmonary artery
distractorRationale.d: The septum is the muscular wall separating the two sides of the heart, not a valve

questions.stem: Veins possess valves along their length whereas arteries do not, because

options.text: blood in veins is at low pressure and would otherwise flow backwards
veins are closer to the skin
veins have thicker walls than arteries

questions.explanation: Blood entering a vein has already lost most of its pressure in the capillaries, so there is little force to keep it moving, especially when it must travel upwards from the legs. Valves close if the blood begins to slip back, so it can only move towards the heart. Arterial blood is under high pressure and cannot reverse.

distractorRationale.a: Oxygen content has no bearing on the need for valves; the pulmonary vein is oxygenated and still has them
distractorRationale.c: Position relative to the skin does not determine backflow
distractorRationale.d: Vein walls are thinner than artery walls, not thicker

questions.stem: Capillary walls are only one cell thick. The main advantage of this is that it

options.text: allows blood to flow very fast
gives a short diffusion distance for the exchange of materials with the tissues
raises the blood pressure in the tissues
prevents white blood cells from leaving the blood

questions.explanation: Exchange occurs by diffusion, and the rate of diffusion falls as the distance increases. A wall of one flattened cell puts the blood almost in contact with the tissue fluid, so oxygen and glucose leave and carbon dioxide and urea enter as quickly as possible.

distractorRationale.a: Blood actually flows most slowly in capillaries, which gives more time for exchange
distractorRationale.c: Pressure falls along a capillary rather than rising
distractorRationale.d: The thin wall lets phagocytes squeeze out to reach infected tissue

questions.stem: What is the main advantage of the double circulation found in mammals compared with the single circulation of fish?

options.text: Less blood is needed in total
Blood is returned to the heart and re-pressurised after the lungs, so it reaches the body tissues quickly
Oxygenated and deoxygenated blood can mix, saving space
The heart needs only two chambers

questions.explanation: Passing through the lung capillaries costs most of the blood's pressure. Because mammalian blood returns to the heart before going to the body, it is given a second push at high pressure, delivering oxygen fast enough to sustain the high metabolic rate of a warm-blooded animal.

distractorRationale.a: Double circulation does not reduce blood volume
distractorRationale.c: The advantage is precisely that the two kinds of blood do not mix
distractorRationale.d: Double circulation requires four chambers; it is fish, with single circulation, that have two

questions.stem: Blood in which vessel would contain the highest concentration of digested food shortly after a meal?
questions.explanation: The hepatic portal vein carries blood directly from the capillaries of the ileum to the liver, so it collects the glucose and amino acids just absorbed from the gut. The liver then regulates these levels before the blood joins the general circulation.

distractorRationale.a: The renal artery branches from the aorta and its food content has already been regulated by the liver
distractorRationale.c: The pulmonary artery carries blood from the right ventricle to the lungs
distractorRationale.d: The vena cava carries mixed blood from the whole body after the liver has adjusted it

questions.stem: All arteries carry oxygenated blood and all veins carry deoxygenated blood.
questions.explanation: False. The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs, and the pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood back. Arteries and veins are defined by direction of flow — away from and towards the heart — not by oxygen content.

questions.stem: The pulse that can be felt at the wrist is caused by

options.text: valves in the veins opening and closing
the elastic wall of an artery stretching and recoiling as a surge of blood passes
blood flowing slowly through the capillaries

questions.explanation: Each contraction of the left ventricle sends a pressure wave along the arteries. The elastic and muscular artery wall stretches to accommodate the surge and then recoils, and that rhythmic expansion is felt as the pulse — which is why a pulse can be taken only over an artery.

distractorRationale.a: Vein valves move quietly and the blood in veins does not pulse
distractorRationale.c: Capillary flow is slow and steady, with no pulse
distractorRationale.d: The atria contract weakly and the wrist pulse follows ventricular contraction

questions.stem: Trace the path of a red blood cell from a capillary in the foot to a capillary in the brain, naming the chambers, valves and vessels it passes through. State one reason why this route is described as a double circulation.
markingGuide: Foot capillary to vein to inferior vena cava (1 mark)
Right atrium, then through the tricuspid valve into the right ventricle (2 marks)
Pulmonary artery to the lung capillaries, where oxygen is taken up (2 marks)
Pulmonary vein to the left atrium, then through the bicuspid valve into the left ventricle (2 marks)
Aorta, then carotid artery, then brain capillary (2 marks)

Reason: the blood passes through the heart twice in one complete circuit — once through the pulmonary circulation and once through the systemic circulation — so it is re-pressurised after the lungs (2 marks)
questions.explanation: The route must show the cell entering the right side of the heart, travelling to the lungs, returning to the left side and only then being sent to the brain. Naming the tricuspid and bicuspid valves in the correct positions is where most marks are gained or lost, and the double circulation point rests on the blood passing through the heart twice per circuit.

questions.stem: Which chamber of the heart receives deoxygenated blood from the body?
questions.explanation: The right atrium is responsible for receiving deoxygenated blood from the body through the superior and inferior vena cavae. This blood is then pumped into the right ventricle, from where it is sent to the lungs for oxygenation.

distractorRationale.a: The left atrium receives oxygenated blood from the lungs, not deoxygenated blood.
distractorRationale.c: The left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood to the body, not receiving deoxygenated blood.
distractorRationale.d: The right ventricle pumps deoxygenated blood to the lungs, not receiving it.

questions.stem: What is the primary function of capillaries in the circulatory system?

options.text: Exchange substances between blood and tissues

questions.explanation: Capillaries are the smallest blood vessels and are designed for the exchange of oxygen, carbon dioxide, nutrients, and waste products between blood and surrounding tissues. This exchange is essential for maintaining homeostasis.

distractorRationale.a: Veins transport blood to the heart, not capillaries.
distractorRationale.c: Capillaries do not store blood; they facilitate exchange.
distractorRationale.d: Blood pressure regulation is primarily the function of arteries and arterioles.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements correctly describes a structural difference between arteries and veins?

options.text: Veins have thicker walls than arteries
Arteries have valves, while veins do not
Arteries have a thicker muscular layer than veins
Veins carry blood away from the heart

questions.explanation: Arteries have thicker muscular walls compared to veins, which allows them to withstand higher pressure as they transport oxygenated blood away from the heart. Veins, in contrast, have thinner walls and valves to prevent backflow.

distractorRationale.a: Veins have thinner walls than arteries.
distractorRationale.b: It is arteries that do not have valves, while many veins do.
distractorRationale.d: Veins carry blood towards the heart, not away from it.

questions.stem: What is the role of the valves in the heart?
questions.explanation: The valves in the heart prevent the backflow of blood, ensuring that it flows in one direction through the heart chambers. This is essential for maintaining efficient circulation and proper functioning of the heart.

distractorRationale.b: Valves do not increase blood pressure; they regulate blood flow direction.
distractorRationale.c: Oxygenation of blood occurs in the lungs, not through the valves.
distractorRationale.d: Nutrient transport occurs through the bloodstream, not via heart valves.

questions.stem: Which blood vessel carries oxygenated blood away from the heart?
questions.explanation: The aorta is the largest artery in the body and carries oxygenated blood from the left ventricle to the rest of the body. This is crucial for delivering oxygen and nutrients to tissues.

distractorRationale.a: The pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart.
distractorRationale.c: The superior vena cava carries deoxygenated blood to the heart.
distractorRationale.d: The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs.

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly describes the flow of blood through the heart?

options.text: Right atrium → Left atrium → Right ventricle → Left ventricle
Left atrium → Right atrium → Left ventricle → Right ventricle
Right atrium → Right ventricle → Left atrium → Left ventricle
Right atrium → Right ventricle → Left ventricle → Left atrium

questions.explanation: Blood flows from the right atrium into the right ventricle before being pumped to the lungs for oxygenation. After returning from the lungs, oxygenated blood enters the left atrium and then flows into the left ventricle.

distractorRationale.a: This sequence incorrectly places the left atrium before the right ventricle.
distractorRationale.b: This sequence incorrectly places the right atrium before the left atrium.
distractorRationale.d: This sequence incorrectly places the left ventricle before the left atrium.

questions.stem: What is the significance of the double circulation system in mammals?

options.text: It allows for separation of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood
It increases the volume of blood in the body

questions.explanation: The double circulation system in mammals separates oxygenated blood from deoxygenated blood, allowing for more efficient oxygen delivery to tissues and organs. This separation is crucial for maintaining a high metabolic rate.

distractorRationale.b: Double circulation does not primarily affect heart rate.
distractorRationale.c: It does not directly increase blood volume; it enhances efficiency.
distractorRationale.d: Blood clotting is regulated by other mechanisms, not by the type of circulation.

questions.stem: Which of the following blood vessels has the thinnest walls?
questions.explanation: Capillaries have the thinnest walls, consisting of a single layer of endothelial cells. This structure facilitates the rapid exchange of gases, nutrients, and waste products between blood and tissues.

distractorRationale.a: Arteries have thicker walls to withstand higher pressure.
distractorRationale.b: Veins have thicker walls than capillaries but are thinner than arteries.
distractorRationale.d: Venules have walls that are thicker than capillaries.

questions.stem: What is the main reason that arteries have thicker walls than veins?
questions.explanation: Arteries have thicker walls to withstand the higher pressure of blood pumped from the heart. This structural adaptation is crucial for maintaining proper circulation and ensuring blood reaches all body tissues.

distractorRationale.a: Arteries carry oxygenated blood, not deoxygenated blood.
distractorRationale.c: Blood clotting is managed by platelets and clotting factors, not wall thickness.
distractorRationale.d: Nutrient exchange occurs in capillaries, not arteries.

questions.stem: In which part of the heart does the oxygenation of blood occur?
questions.explanation: Oxygenation of blood occurs in the lungs, where deoxygenated blood releases carbon dioxide and absorbs oxygen. The oxygenated blood then returns to the heart's left atrium to be pumped to the rest of the body.

distractorRationale.a: The right atrium receives deoxygenated blood, not oxygenated.
distractorRationale.b: The right ventricle pumps deoxygenated blood to the lungs for oxygenation.
distractorRationale.c: The left atrium receives oxygenated blood but does not oxygenate it.

questions.stem: Which blood vessel is responsible for returning deoxygenated blood to the heart?
questions.explanation: Veins are responsible for returning deoxygenated blood to the heart. They carry blood from various parts of the body back to the heart, where it can be sent to the lungs for oxygenation.

distractorRationale.a: The aorta carries oxygenated blood away from the heart.
distractorRationale.b: The pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart.
distractorRationale.d: Arteries carry blood away from the heart, not back to it.

questions.stem: Which structure in the heart prevents the backflow of blood into the atria?

distractorRationale.b: The pulmonary valve prevents backflow into the right ventricle, not the atria.
distractorRationale.d: The bicuspid valve prevents backflow into the left atrium, not the right atrium.

To carry blood away from the heart

questions.explanation: Arteries are responsible for carrying oxygenated blood away from the heart to various parts of the body, except for the pulmonary artery which carries deoxygenated blood to the lungs. This function is crucial for supplying tissues with oxygen and nutrients.

distractorRationale.a: Veins carry blood towards the heart, not arteries.
distractorRationale.c: Capillaries are responsible for the exchange of nutrients and wastes.

options.text: Veins have thicker walls than arteries
Veins have valves to prevent backflow

questions.explanation: Veins have valves that prevent the backflow of blood, ensuring that it moves in one direction back to the heart. This is particularly important in the limbs where blood must travel against gravity.

distractorRationale.a: Arteries have thicker walls than veins due to higher pressure.
distractorRationale.b: Veins typically carry deoxygenated blood, except for the pulmonary vein.

questions.stem: During which phase of the cardiac cycle does the heart muscle contract?
questions.explanation: Systole is the phase of the cardiac cycle when the heart muscle contracts, pumping blood out of the chambers. This is followed by diastole, when the heart muscle relaxes and the chambers fill with blood.

distractorRationale.c: There is no specific resting phase in the cardiac cycle.
distractorRationale.d: The filling phase occurs during diastole, not systole.
